# Jinshu document format

A document is JSON: a `version`, optional metadata, and a list of blocks. Every block has a
`type` and an `id`; list items, table rows, columns and inline atoms have an `id` too. Ids
are unique in the document, and edits address content by id. Agents read and write the same document as
Jinshu Markup, an XML subset that converts both ways without loss.

Rules that hold for every field below:

- An optional field equal to its default is left out, and a `true`-only flag is left out when off.
- Keys the format does not know are kept as they are, so a document from a newer app survives a
  round trip through an older one.
- A document, custom block or inline atom with a `version` newer than this package understands is
  read-only: it renders, and edits to it are refused with problem `VERSION`.
- `update` sets only the fields marked in the `update` column; content changes go through
  `replace` or the text operations.

## Document

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | integer | yes | `1` | ≥ 1 |
| `id` | string |  |  |  |
| `title` | string |  |  |  |
| `lang` | string |  |  |  |
| `meta` | object |  |  |  |
| `blocks` | Block[] | yes |  |  |

## Inline content

`runs`, captions, titles and cells hold a list of inlines. Which kind an inline is follows from the
one key it carries: `text`, `break`, `math` or `inline`.

### Text run

Marks are flat keys on the run, never nested.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  |  |
| `bold` | `true` |  |  |  |
| `italic` | `true` |  |  |  |
| `underline` | `true` |  |  |  |
| `strike` | `true` |  |  |  |
| `code` | `true` |  |  |  |
| `script` | string |  |  | `sub` · `super` |
| `highlight` | string |  |  | `accent` · `warning` · `success` · `danger` |
| `link` | string |  |  | URL or `#block-id` |

### Line break

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `break` | `true` | yes |  |  |

### Inline math

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `math` | string | yes |  |  |

### Inline atom (`x-<scope>-<name>`)

Registered with `defineInline`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | id | yes |  |  |
| `inline` | string | yes |  |  |
| `version` | integer | yes | `1` | ≥ 1 |
| `attrs` | object | yes |  |  |
| `fallback` | string | yes |  |  |

## Markdown

A document can be stored as a Markdown file instead of JSON. The model stays the same; the file holds
the subset ordinary Markdown can say (CommonMark, GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough and autolinks,
`$math$` and `$$` blocks, and the alert syntax for callouts), with no syntax of Jinshu's own. With
`format: 'markdown'`, `checkDocument` and `applyOps` refuse anything outside it with problem
`FORMAT`. Markdown has no ids: reading derives them from content and keeps those of a previous version
for blocks that did not change or stand in the same place.

| Block | Markdown | Not kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paragraph` | Text; an empty paragraph is not written, nor spaces at the edges of a line |  |
| `heading` | `#` to `####` (setext read; `#####` and `######` read as `####`) |  |
| `quote` | `> ` |  |
| `callout` | Alert syntax: `> [!NOTE]` info, `> [!TIP]` tip, `> [!WARNING]` warning, `> [!CAUTION]` danger; no title | `title` |
| `list` | `- ` bullet, `1. ` ordered from `start`, `- [ ] ` / `- [x] ` task when every item has a box; children indented |  |
| `code` | Fenced with backticks and the language; `text` is a bare fence; indented code reads as `text` | `filename`, `highlightLines` |
| `math` | `$$` on its own lines; a `math` fence reads as math too |  |
| `table` | GFM table with its header row (required); `:--` `:-:` `--:` align; no line breaks in cells | `widths` |
| `divider` | `---` |  |
| `image` | `![alt](src)` alone in a paragraph; an empty `alt` is the same as none | `width`, `height`, `caption`, `size` |

Not in Markdown: `details`, `columns`, `video`, `audio`, `file` and custom blocks.

| Mark | Markdown |
| --- | --- |
| `bold` | `**bold**` |
| `italic` | `*italic*` |
| `strike` | `~~strike~~` |
| `code` | `` `code` `` |
| `link` | `[text](url)`, `<url>` and bare URLs |
| `math` | `$latex$` |

Not in Markdown: `underline`, `script`, `highlight`, and inline atoms. A line break is a backslash at the end of the
line.

| Document | Markdown |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | A leading `# Title` line, when it is plain text |
| `meta` | Only `meta.frontMatter`: the file's leading `---` block, kept verbatim |

Not in Markdown: `id`, `lang`.

## Markup

This is the guide the agent tools carry:

```text
Jinshu Markup (strict XML subset, lowercase tags, double-quoted attrs, explicit closing tags).
An attribute has the same name and unit as the JSON field (durationMs="125400", width="480"); lists are comma lists (widths="2,1").
Blocks (attributes in brackets are optional):
  <p id>inline</p>
  <h1..h4 id>inline</h1..h4>
  <quote id>blocks</quote>
  <callout id [tone="info|tip|warning|danger"]><title>inline</title> blocks</callout>
  <details id [defaultOpen]><summary>inline</summary> blocks</details>
  <list id [style="bullet|ordered|task"] [start]><li id [checked="true"]>inline, or <p>inline</p> + child blocks</li></list>
  <code id [language] [filename] [highlightLines]>a ``` fence line, the code, the same fence line (longer fence if the code has ```)</code>
  <math id>LaTeX</math>
  <table id [align="start|center|end"] [widths] [headerRow]><tr id><th|td>inline</th|td></tr> (headerRow="true": the first row is the header)</table>
  <columns id [widths]><col id>blocks</col></columns>
  <divider id/>
  <image id src [alt] [width] [height] [size="small|medium|full"]><caption>inline</caption></image>
  <video id src [poster] [durationMs]><caption>inline</caption> <chapter atMs>title</chapter> <track src lang label/></video>
  <audio id src [title] [cover] [durationMs]><chapter atMs>title</chapter> transcript paragraphs</audio>
  <file id [display="attachment|inline"] src name [mimeType] [sizeBytes] [pageCount] [description]/>
  <x-scope-name id [version] [fallback]><attrs>{JSON}</attrs>inline or block content</x-scope-name> for custom blocks.
Inline: <b>, <i>, <u>, <s>, <code>, <mark [tone="warning|success|danger"]>, <sub>, <sup>, <a href="...">, <br/>, <math>...</math>,
  <x-scope-name id [fallback]/> for an inline atom (echo its id to keep it; add <attrs>{JSON}</attrs> to change it).
Canonical nesting order: a > mark > b > i > u > s > sub/sup > code. Escape only &lt; &gt; &amp; &quot;.
edit matches `find` against the plain text of the field; `replace` is inline markup (plain text keeps the marks at the match).
update sets non-structural fields only; change runs/items/blocks/rows/columns with replace.
```

## Example

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "title": "Week 3: Limits",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "h-intro",
      "type": "heading",
      "level": 2,
      "runs": [
        {
          "text": "What a limit is"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "p-def",
      "type": "paragraph",
      "runs": [
        {
          "text": "A limit describes where "
        },
        {
          "math": "f(x)"
        },
        {
          "text": " is heading",
          "bold": true
        },
        {
          "text": ", not where it is."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "c-note",
      "type": "callout",
      "tone": "tip",
      "title": [
        {
          "text": "Remember"
        }
      ],
      "blocks": [
        {
          "id": "p-note",
          "type": "paragraph",
          "runs": [
            {
              "text": "The function need not be defined at the point."
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "l-tasks",
      "type": "list",
      "style": "task",
      "items": [
        {
          "id": "i-read",
          "checked": true,
          "runs": [
            {
              "text": "Read section 3.1"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "i-try",
          "runs": [
            {
              "text": "Try the exercises"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "t-values",
      "type": "table",
      "headerRow": true,
      "rows": [
        {
          "id": "r-head",
          "cells": [
            [
              {
                "text": "x"
              }
            ],
            [
              {
                "text": "f(x)"
              }
            ]
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "r-1",
          "cells": [
            [
              {
                "text": "0.9"
              }
            ],
            [
              {
                "text": "1.9"
              }
            ]
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "img-graph",
      "type": "image",
      "src": "https://example.com/graph.png",
      "alt": "Graph of f near 1",
      "width": 480,
      "height": 360
    }
  ]
}
```

The same document as markup:

```xml
<doc title="Week 3: Limits">
<h2 id="h-intro">What a limit is</h2>
<p id="p-def">A limit describes where <math>f(x)</math><b> is heading</b>, not where it is.</p>
<callout id="c-note" tone="tip">
  <title>Remember</title>
  <p id="p-note">The function need not be defined at the point.</p>
</callout>
<list id="l-tasks" style="task">
  <li id="i-read" checked="true">Read section 3.1</li>
  <li id="i-try">Try the exercises</li>
</list>
<table id="t-values" headerRow="true">
  <tr id="r-head"><th>x</th><th>f(x)</th></tr>
  <tr id="r-1"><td>0.9</td><td>1.9</td></tr>
</table>
<image id="img-graph" src="https://example.com/graph.png" alt="Graph of f near 1" width="480" height="360"/>
</doc>
```
